payload.text: Make this real react app,

**Designing the Architecture**

I've been mapping out the core components for the React application. The "FlytBase Security Ops" interface will be structured with distinct modules: a dashboard, fleet management, manual control, patrol routes, and incident analysis. Each module will be designed for scalability and seamless integration. My focus is now on establishing the communication protocols between these components.


**Outlining System Configuration**

I'm deep into the design specifics for system settings. Considering aesthetic preferences, dark mode with a cyan/teal accent stands out. I'm choosing status colors for visual clarity, defining typography, and selecting icons. I have a clear file structure in place for the React app, with entry, routing, and component divisions. I'm focusing on defining core pages like the dashboard and fleet management to give context for more specific elements. The aim is to create a structured and intuitive design.


**Developing AI Integration**

I'm now integrating the AI components, focusing on utilizing `@google/genai` through `geminiService.ts`. The initial "Smart Suggestion" feature will provide AI-driven security recommendations based on fleet status and patrol logs. For fleet management, I'll be implementing battery and health charts using `recharts`. Incident analysis will feature a trend vs. SLA bar chart, likely using `d3` or `recharts`, and for manual control, I'm planning to simulate joystick-like UI controls.

Make sure system settings tab has all these featrues

SETTINGS – Full Feature Prompt
Roles & Permissions Sub-section:

Role table showing:

Role name (Field Operator, Team Lead, Director, Admin)

Permission toggles:

Can deploy drones? (yes/no per role)

Can take manual control? (yes/no, and if yes, time limit)

Can approve patrols (esp. emergency)? (yes/no)

Can change alert rules / SLAs? (yes/no)

Can generate & send authority reports? (yes/no)

Can access system settings? (yes/no)

Can declare emergency? (yes/no)

Can request extensions? (yes/no)

Can access analytics? (yes/no)

Edit role button → modal with detailed permission list and scope definition

Add new role button → template + custom permissions

Alert Rules & SLAs Sub-section (NEW: Combined):

Severity levels table:

Critical: 30-second SLA, escalate to Team Lead immediately, auto-dispatch nearest drone

High: 2-minute SLA, escalate to Team Lead after 1:50s, auto-dispatch if no response

Medium: 5-minute SLA, escalate to Supervisor, manual review recommended

Low: 15-minute SLA, monitoring mode, no auto-dispatch

NEW: Threat type responses mapping:

Human Intruder → Critical/High severity, auto-dispatch + emergency protocol option

Environmental (water, fire) → High/Medium, alert building systems

Sensor Fault → Low, log and review pattern

Other → Medium, escalation per operator decision

Confidence & false-alarm thresholds:

Per-sensor threshold sliders (e.g., motion sensor >80% confidence before alerting)

NEW: False alarm feedback loop: after X false alarms from a sensor, auto-raise threshold

Escalation timings:

Auto-dispatch trigger: at [X] seconds for severity [Y]

Team Lead escalation: at [Z] seconds if no response

Director escalation: at [W] minutes if unresolved

Emergency protocol trigger: manual declaration or auto at Director level

Notification preferences per role:

Role dropdown + checkboxes: Email, SMS, Radio, App push

Severity filter: Critical only? All? Medium and above?

Frequency: immediate, digest, batch

Integrations Sub-section:

Card-style list:

Access Control system (status: Connected/Not connected, config button, health indicator)

CCTV platform (status, config, health, feed count)

Incident/ticketing system (status, config, health, sync frequency)

Police/Insurance APIs (if applicable, status, config, health)

Each card shows: integration name, current status, last sync, any error messages, Manage button

Patrol Templates Sub-section:

List of reusable templates with:

Template name

Zone coverage

NEW: Associated threat type (if designed for specific threat response)

Last used date

Template detail/edit: opens map editor similar to Patrols, with NEW: blind spot analysis suggesting improvements

NEW: Smart template suggestions button: AI generates new templates based on incident patterns

Notification Channels Sub-section:

Channel configuration:

Email: server config, test send, delivery confirmation on/off

SMS: provider config, test send, rate limiting

Radio: frequency/channel config, call sign, acknowledging station list

App push: enable/disable, device registration, rate limiting

Appearance Sub-section:

Theme selector: Dark (current default), Light (coming soon)

Density selector: Compact / Normal / Spacious (future)

Language & Region Sub-section:

Language dropdown (English, French, Spanish, German, etc.)

Region/timezone selector

Date/time format preview (e.g., "25 Dec 2025 - 15:30" vs "12/25/2025 - 3:30 PM")

Localization scope: "Apply to my profile only" or "Apply to all operators"

About Sub-section:

Product: "FlytBase Security – Louvre Museum Command Center"

Version (e.g., 1.2.3)

Build number

License type (trial / perpetual / annual)

Last update date and release notes link

Connections:

Role changes → immediately affect what drones appear in Manual Control, which patrols can be approved, which reports can be sent

Alert Rules SLA changes → auto-update Dashboard timers and escalation logic

Threat type responses → feed into incident creation and alert routing

Integrations → status affects Dashboard Connected Systems health

Language change → reload UI in selected language (if multilingual)

Smart template suggestions → pull from Incidents analytics to recommend new patrol patterns

GLOBAL ELEMENTS – Full Feature Prompt
Header (Global):

FlytBase logo + product name "FlytBase Security – Louvre Museum"

Sub-label "Drone Command Center"

NEW: "AI-Assisted" badge (subtle, indicating AI features available)

Search (Global):

Search across: drones (by ID/name), incidents (by title/ID), NEW: guards (by name/ID), patrols (by route name)

Results dropdown showing matched items with category icon and quick action

Notifications Center:

Bell icon with red badge showing unread count

Dropdown showing:

SLA breach alerts (red)

Escalations (orange)

Maintenance due (yellow)

Integration failures (red)

New incidents (blue)

Each notification shows: type, timestamp, related entity link, dismiss/action button

Command Palette / Voice (NEW):

Icon in header (future: activates with keyboard shortcut or voice command)

Allows quick navigation: "Go to Dashboard", "View Incidents", "Deploy Sentinel-1", etc.

NEW: AI-assisted: "What's the status of the museum?" → summarizes alerts, coverage, fleet health

User Profile & Shift Management:

User name and role displayed

Avatar icon

Dropdown menu:

Profile / Account settings

Shift management:

Current shift (time, operator name)

Change shift button → if confirmed, shows handover briefing:

Recent critical incidents (last 2–3)

Active alerts with SLA status

Drones in maintenance or low battery

Coverage gaps flagged

Outstanding reports or escalations

Logout

System Health Widget (Footer/Corner):

Status indicator: Online (green) / Degraded (yellow) / Offline (red)

NEW: Integration health icons:

Access Control: green/yellow/red dot

CCTV: green/yellow/red dot

Sensors: green/yellow/red dot

Tooltip on hover: "System Online – All systems operational" or details of degradation

Click to open brief health report or Settings → Integrations

Connections:

Search → deep-links to relevant detail pages (incident detail, fleet detail, patrol detail)

Notifications → clicking a notification jumps to related screen (Dashboard if SLA breach, Incidents if new incident, etc.)

Command palette → natural language routing to screens + actions

Shift handover → pre-loads Dashboard with context (recent incidents, active alerts, gaps)

System health → links to Integrations settings for troubleshooting

**Developing Comprehensive Features**

I'm currently focused on expanding the "Settings" page and global elements, especially the header, sidebar, and footer. The goal is to build a detailed set of features. Right now, I am specifically thinking about the **header** - I want to include the product name "FlytBase Security – Louvre Museum", and a subheading - "Drone Security Solutions". I plan on implementing an easily customizable logo, ensuring the text labels are readable with accessibility in mind.


**Defining Header Elements**

I've been refining the "Command Center" interface. Key considerations include an AI-assisted badge for quick status assessment, a universal search function across various data points, and a comprehensive notifications center accessed via a bell icon. I'm also exploring a command palette/voice interface for intuitive interaction. Finally, user profiles will contain shift management and handover briefings for efficiency.


**Integrating Enhanced System Controls**

I'm now fully immersed in the "Settings" overhaul, focusing on Roles, Permissions, and refining the System Health Widget. Added new interfaces for core elements in `types.ts`, and I'm updating `Header.tsx` to handle the more complex notification system, search, and handover functionalities.  The `SystemHealthWidget.tsx` component is underway for system monitoring, I'm defining its look and feel.


**Prioritizing New Features**

I'm now zeroing in on high-impact functionalities. Interactive sliders for alert confidence and a grid for mapping threats to severity are front and center. I'm also planning to incorporate polished integration cards with pulse indicators for live health monitoring. Finally, I'm leaning toward a full-screen modal or a large modal for the shift handover briefings, with a comprehensive summary. It's time to build.

I will now implement the requested upgrades for the **Settings** module and **Global Elements**, focusing on high-density data management, the shift handover workflow, and the comprehensive system health infrastructure.

### Technical Specification:

1.  **Global Header & Command**:
    *   Enhanced Search: Logic to categorize results (Drones, Incidents, Guards, Patrols).
    *   Notification Center: A multi-category dropdown handling SLA breaches, escalations, and system failures.
    *   Shift Management: A dedicated "Handover Briefing" modal that synthesizes active gaps and recent critical telemetry.
2.  **Settings Overhaul**:
    *   **Roles & Permissions**: A granular matrix controlling mission-critical actions (e.g., manual override time limits, emergency declaration rights).
    *   **Alert Rules & SLAs**: Mapping of `ThreatType` to response protocols (Auto-dispatch vs. Manual Review) and interactive sensor confidence sliders.
    *   **Integrations**: Status cards for third-party systems (Access Control, CCTV) with health indicators and last-sync timestamps.
    *   **Templates & Localization**: Management of patrol blueprints and global/local localization scopes.
3.  **System Health Widget**: A floating status bar in the corner providing real-time connectivity status for the entire security stack.

payload.text:
Live Alerts – Severity & Confidence Enhancements

For each alert card in the “Live Alerts” panel, apply a severity-based colour system:

Critical: red (#FF4B4B)

High: orange (#FF9F43)

Medium: yellow (#FFC857)

Low: green (#2ECC71)
Use this colour for the severity pill (CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW) and a 2–3 px left border on the card.

Add an AI confidence score to every alert card. This appears in the top-right of the card, replacing the current 00:00 placeholder with a two-line block:

Line 1: SLA label and time (e.g., “SLA: 05:00” or a countdown).

Line 2: Confidence label (e.g., “Conf: 92% (High)”).
The confidence value is colour-coded:

High (80–100%): green text

Medium (50–79%): amber text

Low (0–49%): red text + optional “Potential false” tag.

For alerts with low confidence (<50%), show a “Potential false” indicator on the same row as the confidence, e.g., “Conf: 41% (Low) - Potential false”. This reinforces that the operator should review before dispatching.

Keep the rest of the card layout the same: alert title, location, time (“2m ago”), and assigned asset (“SENTINEL-1”) remain in their current positions. The only structural changes are:

Colour accents on severity and card border.

The confidence + SLA block in the top-right.

Rationale: These changes reduce cognitive load at the moment of alert by making severity and reliability readable in under 1 second (colour + percentage), aligning with the AI-first decision-support goal.

**Revising Alert Styles**

I've been working on styling the "Live Alerts" panel in `Dashboard.tsx`.  My focus is on a severity-based color system, specifically applying different colors to the alert cards based on their criticality. I'm exploring the use of distinct left borders and severity pills. Currently, I'm defining colors for critical and high severity levels and want to expand from there.


**Developing Alert Confidence Indicators**

I'm now integrating confidence scores into the alert system. I've defined a color-coding scheme for confidence levels (green for high, amber for medium, red with a "Potential false" tag for low), and I'm updating `types.ts` to include these. I'm also planning the new layout for the alert cards, including the SLA time, confidence level, and "Potential false" tag where necessary. Next up is mock data updates.


**Incorporating Confidence Levels**

I'm expanding the alert system to include confidence scores. I've updated the `Incident` interface in `types.ts` to include the `confidence` property, which has initiated modifications in `Dashboard.tsx`. I've defined a clear color scheme and layout for confidence level indicators on the alert cards and implemented logic for assigning colors based on confidence scores. Now, I'm working on integrating the new confidence indicators into the card layout, incorporating SLA time and "Potential false" tag.


**Initializing Data Structure**

I'm starting a new phase, which involves updating `types.ts`. I need to reflect a fresh model in the data structure, and after doing so, I'll move on to adjusting the corresponding components.

payload.text:
Multi‑Incident Prioritization in Live Alerts & Map

Extend the Live Alerts panel to support a “multi‑incident mode” when two or more active alerts are present, especially if multiple are CRITICAL or HIGH. When this mode is active, show a compact banner at the top of the Live Alerts stack:

Copy: “🚨 Multi‑incident mode – Prioritizing by zone value and threat severity.”

Always visible above the first alert card while multiple critical/high alerts are active.

For every alert card, compute and display a priority level derived from a simple matrix (Zone criticality × Threat severity). The priority is shown as a small badge near the severity label:

P1 (highest priority) – red badge

P2 – orange badge

P3 – yellow badge

P4 – low priority, muted green
Example: “P1 - CRITICAL” or “P2 - HIGH”.

Sort the alert cards in the Live Alerts panel by priority first, time second:

All P1 alerts at the top (newest first)

Then P2, then P3/P4.
This ensures the operator always sees the most important incident at the top, not just the most recent.

When fleet capacity is limited (e.g., only one drone free) and multiple alerts are active, show assignment status and queueing directly on the cards:

For the alert currently being served: line under the title like “Assigned: SENTINEL‑1 (en route, ETA 01:30)”.

For lower‑priority alerts waiting: “Queued – waiting for drone (est. start in 03:00)”.
Place this line just above the “SENTINEL‑1 / NONE” footer row on each card.

In the map panel, reflect the same priorities:

Use severity colours plus a small priority label (P1/P2/P3) in the incident marker tooltip.
- When Multi‑incident mode is active, draw assignment paths from drones to P1 incidents first, then P2, so it’s visually obvious which incident each drone is handling.

Add a small “Pause routine patrols?” prompt in the Live Alerts header whenever there is at least one P1 incident active:

Two inline buttons: “[Pause patrols]” and “[Keep running]”.

This appears just below the “Multi‑incident mode” banner, and only while P1 is active.

Rationale: These UI elements make concurrent incidents legible at a glance (priority badges + sorted list + queue info), so the operator does not have to manually juggle which alert to handle first or mentally track which incidents are already covered.

**Developing Incident Prioritization**

I'm currently focused on implementing multi-incident prioritization. My key task is updating the `Incident` type within the `Dashboard.tsx` component to include a `priority` level. This will be crucial for the next step, where I'll create the priority matrix. The matrix will consider both `Zone criticality` and `Threat severity` to effectively categorize incidents.

I'm refining the priority matrix considering zone value and threat severity to calculate priority, which will be computed dynamically or pre-calculated in the state. I'm also planning to create a helper function for priority calculations.

I'm now focusing on integrating the priority and assignment status into the incident cards themselves. I've updated the `Incident` type in `types.ts` to include `priority` and `assignmentStatus`. Next, I'll update the mock data and modify the sorting of the `filteredAlerts`. The plan is to enhance the alert cards to display these key incident attributes and ensure the map markers also reflect this information. Additionally, I'll add the "Multi-incident mode" banner and the patrol pause prompt to the UI.

payload.text:
Shift Handover & Context Panel

Add a Shift Briefing dialog that appears whenever a new operator logs in or when the system detects a shift change (e.g., at the start of the night shift). This dialog must appear before the dashboard and requires explicit acknowledgement.

The Shift Briefing content is structured into four sections, stacked vertically inside the modal:

Recent Incidents (last 12 hours): Show a short list (3–5 items) with time, type, zone, severity, and final status (“False alarm – HVAC”, “Resolved in 2:14 by Pierre”).

Fleet Snapshot: Current battery and status for each drone (Active / Idle / Charging / Faulted).

Guard & Patrol Status: Which routes are currently staffed or understaffed, and any coverage gaps (e.g., “Storage Room 4 unpatrolled for 75 min”).

Director / Supervisor Notes: Free‑text notes from Marc or previous supervisor, e.g., “Prioritize West Storage tonight – Picasso delivery; accept slightly higher false‑alarm tolerance there.”

At the bottom of the Shift Briefing modal, add:

A checkbox: “I have reviewed and understood this briefing.”

A primary button: “Acknowledge & go to Dashboard”, disabled until the checkbox is ticked.
This creates an explicit, auditable handover moment.

After the modal is acknowledged, show a persistent shift context bar at the top of the dashboard, directly above the main content:

Left: “Night Shift 22:00–06:00 - Operator: Isabelle”

Middle: key priority pulled from notes, e.g., “Priority zone: West Storage (Picasso)”

Right: two small links: “[View briefing]” (re‑opens modal in read‑only mode) and “[Message previous shift]” (opens chat/notes thread if available).

In the Incidents and Patrols views, add simple filters based on shift:

In the filter bar: a dropdown “Time scope” with options like “Current shift”, “Previous shift”, “Last 24h”.

This sits alongside your existing date range and severity filters.
It allows the night operator to quickly review “What happened in the last shift that matters to me?”

On any open/high‑severity incident that was created in the previous shift, show a small tag near the title:

Example: “Carried over from previous shift”

On hover, show who owned it before and a one‑line note, if available.
This appears in the Incident Detail header, under the title line.

Rationale: These additions keep shift‑critical context (recent incidents, noisy sensors, priority zones, weak patrol coverage) visible at login and lightly persistent in the dashboard. They remove reliance on ad‑hoc verbal handovers and align with the real museum workflow described in the brief.

**Implementing Shift Handoff**

I've been focusing on integrating the "Shift Handover & Context Panel" feature. Currently, the design involves a briefing dialog that appears at login and shift changes.  Users must acknowledge this briefing to proceed to the dashboard. I'm aiming to ensure this workflow is smooth and intuitive within the React application.

Finally, I've decided to place the shift context bar inside the `MainLayout` component to ensure it's displayed correctly.


**Sequencing Modal Displays**

I'm now prioritizing the new `ShiftHandoverModal` and `ShiftContextBar` components, alongside ensuring the previously requested changes are still accurate. I'm focusing on creating those modal sections with incident, fleet, guards, and notes, complete with the acknowledgment checkbox. The context bar's placement is next, either floating or fixed. I also need to ensure incident and patrol filters are time-scoped. Finally, I'll flag carried-over incidents. I'm starting in `App.tsx` and moving to the components.
